text:
tara_docs: I've opened PR #912 to tidy up private/on-prem docs: clearer install ordering, Calico + iptables examples, KMS/HSM wiring, and a PKCS#11 usage snippet. Link: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/912

sam_net: Nice. Which KMS proxy port are we documenting for on-prem? Last week we discussed 8443 for the internal proxy to avoid colliding with existing host services. Also we should include a short checklist for cluster egress NAT testing.

tara_docs: Using 8443 for the local KMS proxy in the docs. HSM vendor TCP is 5696 (we call that out). The PR includes: Calico egress policy with a template variable, an iptables raw table example for baremetal, and a systemd-networkd note. Here's the Calico snippet I'm proposing:

```yaml
apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-hsm-egress
  namespace: redwood-serving
spec:
  selector: app == 'redwood-runtime'
  egress:
  - action: Allow
    protocol: TCP
    destination:
      nets: ["{{HSM_NETWORK_CIDR}}"]  # replace with your HSM VLAN CIDR
      ports: [5696, 8443]
  order: 1000
```

oliver_sec: A few security notes to add: 1) Call out firmware update behavior: many HSMs phone home to vendor update endpoints. For air-gapped installs show how to set VENDOR_UPDATE_URL to empty or point to an internal update mirror. 2) Recommend a dedicated K8s service account like `hsm-client-sa` with minimal RBAC and a pod security policy. 3) Add a short note about requiring time sync between HSM and cluster (NTP) for cert validation.

chris_ops: From operations: some customers hit TLS failures during bootstrap because the docs had them update /etc/hosts before installing the CA bundle. Suggest reorder: 1) Install CA and certs, 2) ensure OS trusts CA, 3) update /etc/hosts or internal DNS, 4) run ./install.sh. I'll paste the failing curl output I saw: `curl: (60) SSL: certificate signature failure` which disappears after the CA bundle is installed.

tara_docs: Good call; I'll reorder the steps. Also added an iptables example for baremetal nodes (raw table to skip conntrack for HSM flows) because of some high-QPS inference setups. Example:

```bash
# iptables: accept HSM TCP directly in raw table to reduce conntrack pressure
iptables -t raw -I PREROUTING -p tcp -d 10.200.5.20 --dport 5696 -j NOTRACK
iptables -t raw -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.200.5.20 --dport 5696 -j NOTRACK
iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp -d 10.200.5.20 --dport 8443 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED -j ACCEPT
```

sam_net: Good. Add a small note to test conntrack size and tune `net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` for high throughput clusters. Also suggest namespace scoping with `namespaceSelector` in docs rather than broad selectors.

oliver_sec: +1. Also include an example one-liner to disable vendor auto-updates for airgapped installs: `echo "VENDOR_UPDATE_URL=" >/etc/hsm/config` (and mention vendor may require a restart).

chris_ops: Can we also include a short PKCS#11 check (no real PINs) and a Python example using `python-pkcs11` showing how to reference the library path from an env var? I threw this together for the PR: 

```bash
# quick pkcs11 smoke test (no PINs in docs)
export PKCS11_LIB=/usr/local/lib/libhsm-pkcs11.so
pkcs11-tool --module "$PKCS11_LIB" --list-slots
```

```python
# pseudo example: use env var for lib path and an external agent for PIN
import os
from pkcs11 import lib
pk11 = lib(os.environ.get('PKCS11_LIB'))
with pk11.get_token(token_label='RedwoodHSM').open(pin_callback=lambda: get_pin_from_agent()) as token:
    key = token.get_key(label='runtime-signing')
    signature = key.sign(b"test")
    print(signature.hex())
```

ci-bot: docs-ci: linkcheck passed ✅, asciidoc build passed ✅, spellcheck ⚠️ 2 warnings (guidance: replace passive voice).

tara_docs: Thanks everyone — I'll: 1) reorder install steps to put CA/certs before hosts changes, 2) add NTP note, 3) swap CIDR to `{{HSM_NETWORK_CIDR}}`, 4) include the conntrack tuning tip, and 5) add the airgap one-liner. Will push updates in the branch and address the spellcheck warnings. Marking PR ready for review after edits.

tara_docs: (follow-up) pushed edits to the branch, removed hardcoded pins in the examples and pointed at an external agent pattern. Ready to merge after CI re-run. :shipit:
